title: Using words instead of hitting
examples: What do I do when I want to hit?
How do I stop myself hitting?
What can I say when I am angry?

explain.say: Sometimes a feeling gets very big. Your hands may want to hit. Lots of people feel that. Look at the board. On the left is hitting. On the right is using words.
The left side is hitting. Hitting hurts someone. They may feel scared. Nobody knows why you feel cross. The problem stays the same. Have your hands ever wanted to hit?
The right side is using words. You can say, I feel cross. Then others understand. You can fix the problem together. Which side helps you get what you need?
Here are the steps. Step 1 is stop. Keep your body still. Step 2 is hands down, by your sides or in your pockets. Step 3 is one slow belly breath. Can you keep your body still right now?

explain.say: The last step is say it. You can say, I feel cross because he took my pencil. Or you can say, Stop, I do not like that. Then get a grown-up. Today, practise stop, hands down, breathe, say it.

faq.q: What do I do when I want to hit?
faq.a: Stop and keep your body still. Put your hands down by your sides or in your pockets. Take one slow breath. Then use words or get a grown-up.

faq.q: What words can I use when I am angry?
faq.a: You can say, I feel cross. You can say, Stop, I do not like that, or I need a break. A grown-up you trust can help.

faq.q: Is it wrong to feel angry?
faq.a: No. Feeling angry is okay. Everyone feels it. Hitting is not okay, because it hurts people. Words help instead.
asks: Am I wrong to be angry?

faq.q: What if I already hit someone?
faq.a: Stop, and get a grown-up. When you are calm, you can say sorry and talk about what to do next time. Everyone can learn.

faq.q: Why do my hands want to hit?
faq.a: Big feelings fill your body with energy. Your hands want to let it out. Squeezing a ball or pushing a wall is a safe way.
asks: Why do I want to hit?

facts: Angry feelings can make the heart beat faster and muscles tighten.
Naming a feeling with words, like I feel cross, can help it settle.

quiz.say: Sam's hands want to hit. What is his first step?
quiz.show: Sam's hands want to hit. What is step 1?
quiz.why: Stopping keeps his hands still, so nobody gets hurt.

wrong.0: Any hitting can hurt, even a soft one.
wrong.1: Shouting can scare people and make the feeling bigger.

quiz.say: Lukas takes Aoife's pencil. What words can she use?
quiz.show: ✏️ Lukas takes Aoife's pencil. What can she say?

options.show: I feel cross. Give it back, please.
options.say: I feel cross. Give it back, please.

quiz.why: Naming her feeling and asking for the pencil helps Lukas understand. Then they can sort it out.

wrong.1: Go away forever can hurt his feelings, and the pencil problem stays.
wrong.2: Calling names can hurt, so naming her own feeling works better.
